info.title: Werft API
info.description:
Private alpha session control plane. This document is generated from the route declarations in apps/control-host/src/api/openapi.ts and the Zod schemas in packages/contracts; do not edit it by hand.

## Authentication

There are two ways to call the API, and they are not interchangeable:

- **Servers and scripts** send an API key as an HTTP bearer token, `Bearer <key>` (`bearerApiKey`). The key is limited to the scopes it was issued with, and it never needs the CSRF header.
- **The web console** uses the browser session cookie that `POST /v1/auth/login` sets (`cookieSession`). What it may do follows the user's workspace role, and every request other than GET must send `X-Requested-With: agent-platform-web` and must not be cross-site (`Sec-Fetch-Site`, `Origin`); otherwise it answers `403 FORBIDDEN`.

An API key cannot manage agents, members, teams or API keys, list agents other than an agent key's own, list or stop sessions through the administration operations, read a session outside its share or take a session over: those operations answer it `403 FORBIDDEN`, whatever its scopes. A missing, malformed, unknown or revoked credential answers `401 UNAUTHORIZED`. `/healthz`, `/readyz`, `/v1/openapi.json`, `/v1/auth/bootstrap` and `/v1/auth/login` take no credential.

## Scopes

Each operation names the one scope it requires, in its description and in its `security` requirement:

- `sessions:read`: read sessions, turns, events, pending requests, usage, limits and receipts.
- `sessions:write`: create sessions and send messages.
- `sessions:approve`: answer pending permission and question requests.
- `sessions:control`: interrupt, pause, resume and terminate.
- `sessions:recover`: record recovery decisions.

What a credential holds:

- An API key holds exactly the scopes it was issued with (`scopes` in `POST /v1/api-keys`, or `--scopes` in the key CLI). A key issued before scopes existed holds none and must be reissued.
- A cookie session holds the scopes of the user's workspace role: `owner` holds all five, `admin` and `member` all but `sessions:recover`.
- A credential without the required scope answers `403 FORBIDDEN` before the body or the resource is read.

## Starting a session with an API key

1. Issue an agent key for the agent with `sessions:write` and `sessions:read`: in the console's API keys screen, or `POST /v1/api-keys` with `kind: "agent"` and its `agent_id`. An owner, an admin or that agent's admin may.
2. `GET /v1/agents` with that key answers its agent alone. Its `active_release_id` is the release to start on; null until the agent is activated.
3. `POST /v1/sessions` with an `Idempotency-Key` and `{"agent_release_id": "<active_release_id>", "message": "..."}`. The release supplies the profile and the repository.
4. `GET /v1/sessions/{id}` follows it.

A personal key with `sessions:write` may start sessions on any agent's release too, but lists no agents: read `active_release_id` from `GET /v1/agents` signed in to the console as an owner or an admin.

## Idempotency

Each command (any method but GET) says in its description whether `Idempotency-Key` is required or ignored. Where it is required, send 1–255 characters; a missing or invalid key answers `400 BAD_REQUEST`. The key is scoped to the caller, the operation and the target resource. Retrying with the same key and the same body returns the original status and body without running the command again; the same key with a different body answers `409 IDEMPOTENCY_CONFLICT`. After a timeout or a lost response, retry with the same key rather than a new one. Where it is ignored, nothing is replayed: a retry runs the command again, so reread the resource before retrying.

## Errors

Every error answers `application/json` with `{"error": {"code", "message", "retryable", "request_id", "details"}}` (`ApiErrorResponse`). Branch on `code`, not on `message`. `retryable: true` means the same request may succeed later unchanged (`REQUEST_TIMEOUT`, `RATE_LIMITED`, `BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE`, `NOT_READY`). Each response below lists its codes and when each one happens.

## Response headers

- `X-Request-Id`: on every response, a fresh id for this request; an error's `request_id` is the same value. Quote it when reporting a problem.
- `Retry-After`: seconds to wait, on `429 RATE_LIMITED` and on `503 BACKEND_UNAVAILABLE`.

tags.name: Health
tags.description: Check process health, readiness and API metadata.

tags.name: Auth
tags.description: Discover the API, sign in (including by redeeming an invite) and manage authenticated browser sessions.

tags.name: Sessions
tags.description: Create sessions and inspect their state and usage.

tags.name: Messages & turns
tags.description: Send session input and inspect turn history and results.

tags.name: Pending requests
tags.description: List and answer pending permission and question requests.

tags.name: Push requests
tags.description: Ask for a session's result to be pushed to its `agent/<session-id>` branch, and approve or reject that push.

tags.name: Session control
tags.description: Stop, pause, resume, close or interrupt a session's execution.

tags.name: Recovery
tags.description: Resolve sessions that require an operator recovery decision. The requester's own decision also takes an API key with `sessions:recover`.

tags.name: Admin
tags.description: See and stop every session of the workspace, read a session outside its share with an audited reason, decide recovery for any session, and take over the sessions of members who were offboarded. Owners and admins, signed in; only an owner decides recovery. Every operation here refuses an API key except the recovery decision, which also takes a key holding `sessions:recover`, but only for sessions the key can already see.

tags.name: Members
tags.description: Invite people, change member roles and issue password reset links. Owners and admins, from a browser session; only an owner grants or changes the owner role or issues a password reset link.

tags.name: Teams
tags.description: Group people into teams; a team named an agent's admin makes every member of it one. Owners and admins change teams, from a browser session. A person added joins at once, without accepting.

tags.name: Agents
tags.description: Write agent cards, release a version against a runtime profile, activate a release and bind the credential names it runs with. Owners, admins, and each agent's own admins.

tags.name: Linked accounts
tags.description: Link and unlink the caller's own Slack account through Sign in with Slack.

tags.name: API keys
tags.description: Issue and revoke keys, never above what the issuer holds. Signed-in people only.

tags.name: Limits & receipts
tags.description: Inspect installation limits and asynchronous command receipts.

RequestId.description: A fresh id for this request, on every response; an error body's `request_id` carries the same value.

RetryAfter.description: Seconds to wait before sending the same request again.

profile_id.description: The catalog profile the session runs on. Required without `agent_release_id`; with it, omitted means the release's profile, and sent it must be that profile.

title.description: The session's name. Omitted, it is derived from `message`: whitespace and line breaks collapsed to one space, the ends trimmed, and text longer than 80 characters cut to 79 and an ellipsis (…). Rename it later with `PATCH /v1/sessions/{id}`.

repository_id.description: The catalog repository the session works on. Required when the profile's `repository_mode` is `required`, refused when it is `none`, either when it is `optional`; omitted, the session works on the release's `repository_id` when `agent_release_id` is sent, else starts in an empty workspace with no repository to push to.

model.description: One of the models the profile offers (its `model` or one of its `models` in the catalog). Omitted, the model of the agent release's card when `agent_release_id` is sent, else the profile's default `model`. Kept until the session's profile is changed, after which the new profile's default `model` runs.

permission_wait.description: How long the session's permission and question requests wait for an answer, in seconds: `park_after_seconds` before the platform parks the turn and frees its worker (0 parks at once), `expire_after_seconds` from the request until it stops taking answers and is denied. Each can only shorten the profile's value (`GET /v1/profiles`, `permission_wait`); a longer one is 400 `PERMISSION_WAIT_ABOVE_PROFILE`. Omitted, the profile's values apply. A request takes the values in force when it is raised.

status.description: Filters on the status each item reports, needs_input included as derived when read.

agent_id.description: Keeps the sessions created for this agent, whichever of its releases they are pinned to. An agent with no session the caller can read, or no such agent, gives an empty page.

relation.description: Narrows the sessions the caller can read, never widens them; omitted, `all`. `started`: the caller started it (for an API key, the key or the person who created it). `shared`: someone else's session shared with the caller by name or through a team the caller is a member of; sessions every workspace member sees appear only under `all`. `administered`: a session of an agent the caller administers, directly or through a team.

q.description: Matches a session whose title contains it, ignoring case, or whose id starts with it.

status.description: needs_input is derived when read: a running session or turn with at least one pending request a client can still answer (open, unexpired, raised by the attempt that holds the turn), or an idle session whose turn was parked on requests still open (`input_wait.state: parked`). state.description: `waiting`: a worker holds the turn open on the requests. `parking`: the platform is pausing the session to free its worker, and an answer can still reach the turn before it stops. `parked`: the turn stopped with its checkpoint and the session is paused; answering resumes it. `expired`: every request the parked turn waited on expired unanswered; the session stays paused until someone resumes it.

post.summary: Durably accept a session and its first input
post.description:
Creates a session for a catalog profile and repository and queues `message` as turn `1`. Whether `repository_id` is sent follows the profile's `repository_mode` (`GET /v1/profiles`): `required` needs it, `none` refuses it, `optional` takes either; a session created without one starts in an empty workspace, has no repository to push to (`POST /v1/sessions/{id}/push-requests` answers 409 PUSH_SOURCE_MISSING) and its detail's `repository_id` is null. The 201 means the input is stored, not that it ran: follow the turn with `GET /v1/sessions/{id}/turns/{turn_id}` or the event stream. `model` picks one of the models the profile offers (its `model` or `models` in the catalog); omitted, the model of the release's card runs when `agent_release_id` is sent, else the profile's default. The session's detail reports it as `model`. The model stays until the session's profile is changed (`POST /v1/sessions/{id}/profile`), which runs the new profile's default. A session waits in `queued` while no execution slot is free; it is never refused for that. `agent_release_id` pins the session to that release of an agent, so a key bound to the agent may create it (it reads the agent's `active_release_id` from `GET /v1/agents`);`profile_id` may then be omitted for the release's runtime profile, and sent it must be that profile (409 RELEASE_PROFILE_MISMATCH). Omitted, `repository_id` is the release's `repository_id`. A release whose profile is no longer in the catalog, or changed since, answers 409 PROFILE_DIGEST_MISMATCH. A profile the operator blocked, or a workspace profile over a blocked one, answers 409 PROFILE_BLOCKED, with a release or without. Every credential the release names must still be bound to its agent; otherwise 409 CREDENTIAL_UNBOUND, whose `details` carry the guidance to show the requester and the agent's admins to ask (`SessionCredentialUnboundDetails`), never the missing names. The receipt settles with turn `1`: `succeeded` when it completes, `failed` when it fails or is interrupted or cancelled, `unknown` when its outcome is unknown.

get.description:
Streams the session's events as Server-Sent Events: first the stored events after `Last-Event-ID` (all of them without it), then new ones as they are written. Each frame's `id` is its cursor, `event` its kind (`system`, `assistant`, `tool_use`, `tool_result`, `question`, `result`, `status`, `error`), and `data` a versioned envelope naming the session, turn and attempt. Frames arrive in `id` order, the order to rely on; a new event's `occurred_at` is no earlier than the one before it. An event the engine emits after its turn's terminal belongs to no turn (`turn_id` null). `question` events announce pending requests; `status` events report the session's status and, after a pause, resume, terminate or recovery decision, its `admission_state`. `system` events with a platform `subtype` are the control plane's own: `session_closed` when a close commits, and `input_wait` with `stage` (`parked` when a turn parks on its unanswered requests, `expired` when a parked turn's requests expire, `lost` when the worker holding them went away unanswered) and the `request_ids` it covers. The stream does not end with a turn or the session: it stays open until the client disconnects, the credential is revoked, or the session's share stops covering the caller (the reconnect then answers 404). Reading changes nothing.

Reconnect after backoff with the last complete event id in `Last-Event-ID`; replay resumes strictly after that event. The stream sends a comment keepalive every 15 seconds. `410 CURSOR_EXPIRED` means the cursor fell outside retained history and the client must resynchronize from resource state; alpha does not trim events, so this response is reserved. A `result` event is engine output, not durable completion: confirm the turn with `GET /v1/sessions/{id}/turns/{turn_id}` and treat only `completed`, `failed`, `interrupted`, `cancelled`, or `outcome_unknown` as terminal.

The agent needs an active release. Installing it into Slack starts at `POST /v1/agents/{id}/slack/install/start`. post.description:
The console's callback page sends the `state` and the `code` (or Slack's `error`) from Slack's redirect, with the agent it is for. The state is spent first, whatever happens next: unknown, spent, expired, or issued to another caller, workspace, agent or app answers 409 SLACK_INSTALL_STATE_INVALID with `error.details.reason_code`. An `error` from Slack (e.g. `access_denied`) answers 409 SLACK_INSTALL_DENIED. The code is exchanged with `oauth.v2.access`; unless the answer names the agent's app, the workspace's Slack team, no enterprise install and every bot scope, nothing is stored (409 SLACK_INSTALL_REJECTED). Then the bot token is sealed under the app (never returned), the install is verified with the token itself (`auth.test` and `bots.info`), the agent's identity is linked, and the steps after an install run; `finalized: false` says those failed and the install stands. Installing again with a new link replaces the bot token and keeps the one install. Every answer carries `Referrer-Policy: no-referrer`. Owners, admins and the agent's admins from a signed-in console; API keys are refused. A new identity writes a `link_agent_identity` receipt.

get.summary: Cost, tokens and run time of the sessions created in a period
get.description:
Adds up the sessions created in `[since, until)`: how many, their estimated provider cost, their tokens, and how long their turns ran. `since` and `until` take a date (`2026-10-01`, that day's 00:00 UTC) or a timestamp with an offset, which is moved to UTC; without `until` the period ends when the figures are read, so `since` must then be in the past.

- `scope=me`: the sessions the caller started. A personal API key counts as the person who created it; a key nobody created counts the sessions it started itself. Sessions shared with the caller are not added. A key bound to an agent gets 403, as it does from `GET /v1/sessions`.
- `scope=installation`: every session of every owner. Only the workspace owner, signed in, reads it: any other member and every API key get 403.
- `scope=agent` with `agent_id`: the sessions started from any release of that agent, whoever started them. The workspace's owner and admins and the agent's admins read it; anyone else, and every API key, gets 403, and an agent of another workspace, or none, is 404 for everyone. `agent_id` is required with it and refused with any other scope, and `group_by` is refused with it.

`cost_usd` is the sum of `cost.amount_usd` from `GET /v1/sessions/{id}/usage` over the same sessions: an estimate, not a bill. `cost_complete: false` means one of them has a turn still open or one that ended without reporting its cost, so the true total is unknown. `run_seconds` is wall-clock turn time, waiting for an answer included; an open turn counts up to `refreshed_at`. Sessions from before tokens were metered count 0 tokens.

`group_by=agent`, `group_by=user` or `group_by=profile` adds `groups`: the same sessions, each once, under its agent, the user holding it or the session's current profile (`sessions.profile_id`; a session that changed profile counts whole under the one it has now), largest cost first, read in the same statement as the totals. The groups' `session_count`, `cost_usd` and `run_seconds` add up to the totals (`run_seconds` is the floor of the running total minus the floor of the one before it, so two groups of 1.5 seconds read 1 and 2), and `cost_complete` is false when any group's is. `id` is the agent id, user id or profile id; it is null for sessions without an agent or a profile, or started by a key no person created. `name` is the agent's name, the user's display name (never an email) or, as profiles have no display name, the profile id; under `scope=me` a user other than the caller is null.
